classification.difficultyReason: The student must devise an inscribed equilateral-triangle construction without intermediate prompts, connecting equal radii and triangle angles to suitable compass constructions, such as bisecting constructed 60-degree angles.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Construct a large circle with centre $O$.

answer.worked: Mark $O$. Set the compasses to a suitable radius and draw a complete circle centred at $O$. Keep this drawing for part b.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Using ruler and compasses only, construct an equilateral triangle $ABC$ in which all three vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on the circle.

answer.short:
An equilateral triangle $ABC$ inscribed in the circle.

Draw radius $OA$ and construct a $30^{\circ}$ angle on each side of $AO$ at $A$. The rays meet the circle again at $B$ and $C$; join $BC$.
answer.worked:
Choose $A$ on the circle and draw $OA$. At $A$, construct a $60^{\circ}$ angle with arm $AO$ on each side of $AO$, using equal-radius compass arcs. Bisect each angle to obtain two rays making $30^{\circ}$ with $AO$. Label their second intersections with the circle $B$ and $C$, and join $AB$, $AC$ and $BC$.

Since $OA=OB$, the base angles of $\triangle AOB$ are equal, so $\angle ABO=30^{\circ}$. Similarly, $\angle ACO=30^{\circ}$. Thus
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=30^{\circ}+30^{\circ}\\\angle BAC&=60^{\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
The remaining angles of $\triangle BOC$ are equal because $OB=OC$. Together with the equal $30^{\circ}$ angles above, this gives $\angle ABC=\angle ACB$. The angle sum of $\triangle ABC$ then gives $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=60^{\circ}$. All three angles are equal, so all three sides are equal.

spec.description: Authored completed construction showing the common circle, centre O, inscribed equilateral triangle ABC and the two constructed 30-degree angles at A.
spec.mathematics: A, B and C lie on the circle; angle BAO and angle OAC are each 30 degrees, giving three equal triangle angles.
